entry.title: Replace bundled country boundaries with the unmodified Natural Earth …
entry.content:
Replace bundled country boundaries with the unmodified Natural Earth file

Memor/Resources/world_countries.geojson (a bare [{name, geometry}] array
with no provenance) is replaced by ne_50m_admin_0_countries.geojson: the
unmodified Natural Earth "Admin 0 – Countries" 1:50m v5.1.2 GeoJSON
FeatureCollection (public domain), credited in ATTRIBUTIONS.md with the
upstream tag and SHA-256. The old file turns out to have been exactly
this dataset reduced to NAME_EN + geometry — the new seed yields the
same 242 names and identical geometry — so a fresh database matches an
existing one.

The seeder now parses the file through parseUploadedBoundaryFile (which
gains a `nameProperty` parameter, default "name"; the seed passes
NAME_EN), so it accepts a FeatureCollection and wraps the 123 plain
Polygon features Natural Earth ships — the old strict Decodable shape
would have failed on those. Set + boundary insertion is factored into
insertBoundarySet, shared with user uploads; NormalizedGeometry moves
beside it. Seeding is still a one-time no-op once a built-in set
exists, so existing databases are untouched.

Verified with a scratch harness running the extracted parser over the
new file (242 features, name set and geometry equal to the old file,
default key correctly rejects it) and a Debug build (new resource
copied, stale world_countries.geojson removed from the bundle).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Local file scheme: quote-aware URL matching so apostrophes in filenam…
entry.content:
Local file scheme: quote-aware URL matching so apostrophes in filenames survive

rewriteLocalFileResourceURLs stopped its match at either quote, so a file URL
containing an apostrophe (file URLs keep ' literal; song titles carry them)
was only half-rewritten: the head was encoded, the tail spliced back raw, and
a later & or %23 in the tail became a live delimiter after the handler's single
decode - "Rock 'n' Roll & Blues.mp3" resolved to "Rock 'n' Roll " and
"Don't #1.mp3" to "Don't ". The terminator now depends on the delimiter: only
" ends a match inside a double-quoted attribute (what the editor inserts), only
' inside a single-quoted one, either for a bare URL. Verified by a scratch
round trip of both names plus the earlier & / unicode / # / % cases; CLAUDE.md
records the whole-URL + delimiter-encoding invariant. Pre-existing for images.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: QueryHTMLView: play-first-audio request nonce
entry.content:
QueryHTMLView: play-first-audio request nonce

Adds the only Swift-to-page seam the query web views have: a
playFirstAudioRequestID nonce prop (same shape as the PointMap locator pulse).
Each fresh id makes QueryWebContainerView evaluate a script that restarts and
plays the FIRST <audio> in document order; ids are deduped, seeded on container
creation so a stale id never fires on mount, parked until the current load
commits (the script itself waits for DOMContentLoaded while parsing), and
cleared when new HTML arrives. Media is paused when the container leaves its
window and when its window closes - the Query Preview is a Window scene, so
closing it never unmounts the view. Debug builds make the web view inspectable
so the handler's Range/206 traffic can be checked in Safari's Web Inspector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Local file scheme handler: HTTP responses with byte-range (206) support
entry.content:
Local file scheme handler: HTTP responses with byte-range (206) support

The flashcards-local-image handler answered every request with a plain
URLResponse holding the whole file: no status code, no headers, Range ignored.
Images never cared, but WebKit's AVFoundation-backed <audio> loader issues
Range requests and needs 206 + Content-Range (and Accept-Ranges) to play and
seek. Answer with HTTPURLResponse everywhere: 200 whole file, 206 for a
satisfiable single range, 416 when unsatisfiable, Content-Range derived from
the bytes actually read. Only the requested slice is read, via FileHandle
under withSecurityScopedFileAccess, so ranged requests no longer re-read whole
files. Delivery stays synchronous, which is why stop() stays a no-op.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: AppDatabase: closure-based security-scoped file access (behavior-pres…
entry.content:
AppDatabase: closure-based security-scoped file access (behavior-preserving)

readSecurityScopedFile(at:) always read the whole file into Data. Generalize
the same three-tier scope logic (retained scope -> re-resolved bookmark with
stale refresh -> unscoped) into withSecurityScopedFileAccess(at:_:), which runs
a caller-supplied closure under the scope so the scheme handler can soon open a
FileHandle and read only a byte range. The handler's one call site passes
{ try Data(contentsOf: $0) }, so nothing changes yet. Doc comments record that
grantImageFileAccess / image_file store bookmarks for ANY user-picked file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Local file scheme: percent-encode the file URL so "&" in filenames su…
entry.content:
Local file scheme: percent-encode the file URL so "&" in filenames survives

rewriteLocalFileResourceURLs carried the original file:// URL as one query-item
value encoded with .urlQueryAllowed, which leaves & + = literal. A filename
containing "&" therefore split the value at that character, the handler saw a
truncated URL, and the read failed. Encode those three delimiters too; the
handler already decodes via URLComponents.queryItems, so nothing else changes.
Pre-existing for images; common in music filenames, so it would bite audio.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: PointMap reverse queries: show the locator mini-map once the answer i…
entry.content:
PointMap reverse queries: show the locator mini-map once the answer is revealed

The bottom-left zoomed-in inset (query point in red) used to be forward-only.
On a Name->Point query it now appears after the user answers, and stays off
before that so it can't give the point away. The inset stays MOUNTED for
every query with a highlighted point and is hidden via opacity instead of
being unmounted: its MKMapView leaks VectorKit resources on teardown, and a
reverse-only stack would otherwise rebuild it on every reveal/advance.

entry.title: Study mode: magenta locator rings on every advance to a PointMap forw…
entry.content:
Study mode: magenta locator rings on every advance to a PointMap forward query

Three concentric magenta rings appear around the query point and fade out
(1 - t^2) over one second whenever Study mode advances to a PointMap
Forward query, so the eye lands on the point immediately. The pulse is
driven by a fresh `pointMapLocatorPulseID` from loadNextQuery (nil for
other kinds and on rating undo), so re-advancing after Cmd+Z pulses again
while undoing back to an already-seen query does not. The map coordinator
now reports the answer point's position for forward queries pre-reveal
too (`tracksAnswerPosition`); the tooltip keeps its own post-reveal gate,
and reverse queries never report or pulse.
